subject: science
passage: On a few beaches along the coast of Odisha, in eastern India, olive ridley sea turtles nest in a remarkable way. Instead of arriving one by one, tens of thousands of females may come ashore over just a few nights to dig nests and lay eggs, an event known by the Spanish word arribada, or "arrival." <u>Biologists think this crowding may help the eggs survive, since predators such as jackals and crows can eat only a small share of so many eggs at once.</u> Exactly what signals the turtles to gather at the same time, however, is still not understood.
stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

choices.A: It describes how quickly the turtles arrive on the beaches.
choices.B: It suggests a possible reason for the behavior described just before it.
choices.C: It identifies the signal that causes the turtles to arrive together.
choices.D: It argues that predators are the greatest threat to the turtles' survival.

explanation.why: The sentence before the underlined one describes the behavior: thousands of turtles nesting "over just a few nights." The underlined sentence gives a possible benefit of that crowding, hedged with "think" and "may": predators can eat only a small share of the eggs. The last sentence then notes what is still unknown.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The speed of the arrival is described in the previous sentence; the underlined sentence suggests why the crowding helps.
explanation.B: Correct. It offers a likely reason for mass nesting: so many eggs at once means predators can eat only a small share.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The last sentence says the signal "is still not understood," so the underlined sentence cannot identify it.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The sentence names predators but does not compare them with other threats, so this claims more than the text.
